summary: The South-South Cooperation scholarships of the Republic of Chile are run by AGCID, the Chilean government's international cooperation agency, and pay for master's (magister) studies at accredited Chilean universities and other higher education institutions from the 2027 academic year. They are for professionals of Latin American and Caribbean countries named in the call, with priority for public officials and university academics. Applications are not sent to AGCID directly: they go through each country's government focal point, with a copy to the Chilean embassy. The award covers tuition, a monthly allowance, insurance and two smaller grants for up to 24 months.
eligibility_notes:
The call invites professionals who are nationals of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Panama, the Dominican Republic and the CARICOM members Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, Montserrat, Saint Lucia, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago. The AGCID programme page lists Colombia, Mexico and Peru under a separate Pacific Alliance track, so applicants from those three countries should check which track applies.

Applicants need a professional title or academic degree, and must obtain an unconditional, definitive acceptance into a master's programme of the call's Annex 1 list at a Chilean institution on their own, at their own cost. A programme not on the list is not considered. The study must be full-time with exclusive dedication, and in-person or hybrid study that keeps the scholar in Chile for the whole programme gets priority. The programme page says non-Spanish speakers must prove Spanish; the call text read does not give a test or score.

The call gives priority to candidates presented by public officials or by academics of universities recognised by their country, to programmes in the Annex 1 list, and to postgraduate programmes in themes Chile considers relevant: astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energy, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, sovereignty and national security, and the fight against organised crime and terrorism. The consular notice says the scholarships are for people working in the public sector, the academic sector or civil society.

Not accepted: foreigners who already hold a residence or work visa for Chile; applicants whose spouse holds this or another AGCID scholarship (if spouses both apply, only one can get an award). The scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarship the person holds in Chile. A former AGCID postgraduate scholar must wait five years after the end of the earlier scholarship before applying for a new postgraduate scholarship (three years for a short specialised course). AGCID's programme page says MBAs and medical specialisations are not funded.
age_experience_notes: No minimum or maximum age and no minimum years of experience are required by the call. Age and work experience only change the score: age groups 36 to 50 score highest (100 points), under 36 score 50 and over 50 score 20; professional experience in the field of the programme scores 100 points for 5 years or more, 65 for 3 years to under 5, 35 for 6 months to 3 years, and 5 below 6 months. The programme page describes the target group as people with prior work experience.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays tuition, enrolment and graduation costs of the programme (up to four academic semesters or six trimesters), a monthly maintenance allowance of CLP 600,000 for up to 24 months, life, health and accident insurance valid in Chile, a one-time study materials grant of CLP 90,000, and a one-time thesis support grant of CLP 300,000. The call lists these benefits as the only ones. Flights to Chile, visa costs, application costs to universities, airport taxes and trips home are the scholar's own cost. The scholarship lasts up to 24 months depending on the programme length, with studies starting between 1 March and 30 September 2027.
programmes_note: Only full-time master's programmes on the call's Annex 1 list, run by accredited Chilean institutions, can be funded; there is no other subject restriction in the call apart from the priority themes (astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energy, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, sovereignty and national security, and the fight against organised crime and terrorism). The programme page says MBAs and medical specialisations are not funded and that in-person or hybrid programmes are preferred. The list itself (Annex 1) was not part of the call text that could be read, so no individual programmes are listed here.
institutions_note: Accredited Chilean universities and other higher education institutions that offer the master's programmes on the Annex 1 list. Applicants contact the admissions staff of the university themselves and should ask in writing about entry requirements, prior skills, emphasis and the curriculum. Applications to universities in regions of Chile (outside Santiago) score higher in selection (100 points against 50 for Santiago).

summary.detail: Master's (magister) programmes from the Annex 1 list at accredited Chilean institutions, taught in Spanish, full-time with exclusive dedication, up to 24 months of funding. Studies may start from 1 March to 30 September 2027. Requires a professional title or degree and unconditional acceptance into the programme. The listing for the 2027 call on the AGCID site gives the study period as 3 March 2027 to 28 February 2029 (carried over from stored data).

benefits.limit_text: Tuition, enrolment and graduation costs charged by the institution, up to four academic semesters or six academic trimesters
benefits.conditions: Only costs of the academic curriculum of the programme for which the scholarship was granted.

benefits.limit_text: CLP 600,000 per month, for the length of the programme and up to 24 months
benefits.conditions: Paid from the month studies start. In December, January and February, the scholar needs AGCID's approval of any trip out of the country to get 100% of that month's allowance. Not paid to scholars who study fully online.

benefits.limit_text: Life, health and accident insurance for events inside Chile while the scholarship lasts; access to Chile's public health services once the scholar has the Chilean national identity card
benefits.conditions: Not applicable to scholars who study fully online. Travel insurance for the flights is advised but not provided.

benefits.limit_text: One-time grant of CLP 90,000 for books and study materials
benefits.conditions: Paid within the first academic period. Not for fully online scholars.

benefits.limit_text: One-time thesis support grant of CLP 300,000
benefits.conditions: Paid if the grade average in the programme is 5.5 or higher (or equivalent). Before the end of the 19th month of the allowance the scholar must show the signed thesis schedule, the approved thesis project and a grade certificate.

benefits.limit_text: Flights to Chile and trips home during the scholarship are not paid
benefits.conditions: Also not paid: visa procedures, application costs to Chilean institutions, airport boarding taxes and similar charges. Anything not listed as a benefit is the scholar's cost.

requirements.text: Application form for the AGCID scholarship, filled in on a computer and signed (Annex 4).

Definitive acceptance letter from the Chilean institution, issued by the competent authority, showing unconditional acceptance, the study mode (in person, hybrid or online), start and end dates of the master's including thesis and final exam, and the enrolment fee and annual tuition. The cost of getting the letter is the applicant's.
Health certificate from a licensed doctor listing pre-existing conditions declared by the applicant (the call's Annex 5 declaration form is attached); needed for the insurance AGCID buys.
Original professional title certificate or a copy certified by a notary. If selected, it must be apostilled or legalised in the country that issued it.
CV with emphasis on work and academic background.
Motivation letter giving the reasons for studying in Chile, the aims of the studies and how they will be applied after returning home.
Short description of the likely thesis area and topic.
Sponsorship letter from the employer, stating the employer's interest in the studies in Chile and that the employee has permission to be absent for the whole scholarship.
Excel sheet with required information about the master's programme and the scholar (the call's registration sheet).

All documents are sent electronically, scanned and legible, to the home country's focal point with a copy to the Chilean embassy; the focal point enters them into AGCID's scholarship platform. The same rules apply, where relevant, to foreigners already studying in Chile (without a residence or work visa).

application_steps.title: Get unconditional acceptance in an Annex 1 master's programme
application_steps.detail: Handle the admission yourself, at your own cost, with the Chilean institution, and ask the admissions staff in writing about requirements, prior skills, emphasis and curriculum. You need the definitive acceptance letter showing the study mode, dates, enrolment fee and annual tuition. A programme not on the Annex 1 list will not be considered.

application_steps.title: Prepare the documents and send them to your focal point
application_steps.detail: Send the full electronic file (form, acceptance letter, health certificate, title, CV, motivation letter, thesis description, academic reference, employer letter if employed, and the Excel sheet) to your country's government focal point and a copy to the Chilean embassy. AGCID does not take individual applications; the focal point sets its own national deadline, which you must check, and verifies you meet the requirements. A missing document or a false document eliminates the application.

application_steps.title: The focal point enters pre-selected candidates in AGCID's platform
application_steps.detail: Focal points upload the officially presented candidacies in AGCID's scholarship management platform, with a ranked list and a record of the pre-selection. The platform deadline for the 2027 call was 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Chile time; entries after that are automatically excluded.

application_steps.title: National pre-selection by focal point and Chilean embassy
application_steps.detail: A joint committee of the focal point and an official of the Chilean embassy chooses candidates on technical criteria; it may interview applicants. Each country ranks its candidates from first priority downwards, and they compete for places with the pre-selected candidates of the other participating countries.

application_steps.title: Final selection by AGCID's committee in Chile
application_steps.detail: The selection committee in Chile scores the candidates on these weights: country priority 20%, alignment with Chile's foreign policy priorities 15%, work experience 25%, type of employer 10%, gender 10% (women score higher), age 5% and region of the Chilean university 5%, then gives an overall judgement. A tie goes to programmes starting in the first semester. The decision cannot be appealed, and results were announced from the second half of November 2026, to applicants and to both countries' ambassadors.

application_steps.title: Sign the scholarship acceptance document and get the visa
application_steps.detail: The award takes effect when the scholar signs AGCID's acceptance document. Get the employer's permission if employed, and apply for the student visa online straight after selection: it can take up to two months, and no one without the approved visa resolution can enter Chile. You can start the visa once you hold the definitive acceptance letter, which does not oblige AGCID to give you the scholarship. Visa costs are the scholar's.

application_steps.title: Arrive, settle and meet the scholar's duties
application_steps.detail: Scholars must set a home address in the study city within three working days of arrival, study exclusively and not take paid work in Chile, pass all courses with a grade average of at least 5.0 each period, ask AGCID for authorisation before leaving Chile (only in the December to February academic holiday or for up to five working days), provide thesis copy at the end and acknowledge AGCID in publications. Failing courses can suspend the allowance, serious breaches end the scholarship and may require repayment.

application_steps.title: Finish the programme and return home
application_steps.detail: The scholar must complete the full programme and return to the home country afterwards. Early end of the scholarship by changing programme without approval, serious breach or serious university sanction bars the person from future AGCID scholarships and requires repaying benefits other than insurance; a scholar who finishes must wait five years before a new AGCID postgraduate scholarship.

not_stated: The Annex 1 list of eligible master's programmes and institutions, and the Annex 3 list of focal points and their national deadlines: not included in the call text read, and the AGCID current-offers page showed no annexes.
A minimum Spanish test or score: the programme page says non-Spanish speakers must prove Spanish, but the call text read gives no test or score.
A minimum grade average for applicants, and the number of scholarships per country or in total.
A maximum age or minimum years of work experience (age and experience only affect the score).
A closing time for national applications: set by each focal point.
fetch_problems: The AGCID current-offers page showed no call details or annexes when read, and the convocatorias page only loads its content by script.
Annexes 1 to 5 and the Excel registration sheet were not available as separate files, so the programme list and the focal point list are not read.
notes: The 2027 call text lists Colombia, Mexico and Peru among the invited nationalities, while the AGCID programme page places those countries in a separate Pacific Alliance track (which also pays round-trip flights between the capital and Santiago). Editors may want to check which track applies.
The selection weights listed in the call add up to 90%, although the call writes a total of 100%.

The study period in the stored milestone (3 March 2027 to 28 February 2029) comes from the AGCID site listing and was not re-read; the call itself says studies may start between 1 March and 30 September 2027.
The stored amounts (CLP 600,000, 90,000 and 300,000) and the tuition limit match the 2027 call text; the earlier 'based on the 2026 call text' remarks are now confirmed by the 2027 call.
The tie-break rule in the 2027 call text still mentions programmes starting in the first semester of 2026 (an apparent leftover from the previous call); it is described here as the first semester.
